description:
An inbox fills up whether you look at it or not. Dev-tool alerts that actually need a fix. Newsletters you never asked twice for. Notification spam wearing a real sender's name. Sorting it by hand is the same ten minutes every day, spent the same way.

Siftbox connects to your Gmail and reads your actual inbox, not a copy of it. Every message gets scored before anything happens to it: sender/domain mismatch, urgency language, an unsubscribe header nobody asked for. Two or more signals means junk.

Once something's flagged, clearing it is one tap. Unsubscribe sends a real RFC 8058 one-click request straight to the sender, the same standard every major mail provider supports, so nothing gets left half-cleared. Archive and delete are just as direct. Nothing happens until you tap it.

Sign in with Google, and Siftbox is ready. Same experience on web, iPhone, and Mac.
promotionalText: Connect Gmail. Siftbox scores the junk and clears it in one tap.
